**Slide 2: Hormone curve illustration**
- Background: cream (#F5F1EC).
- Centred clinical line-graph illustration (no photo — illustrative, editorial style). Show two overlaid hormone curves:
  - Progesterone curve in soft sage green (#A8B8A8 or a muted green-grey harmony with EHN green #39B54A).

  - Y-axis unlabelled (clinical aesthetic; matches winner).
  - Image credit in light grey text (~24px Satoshi Medium, justified right or left, no visual weight).

**Slide 3: Symptom callouts**
- Background: cream (#F5F1EC).
- Three stacked callout blocks, each with a small icon (line-drawn, editorial style: flame for anti-inflammatory, smiley for mood, down-arrow for histamine), followed by a short phrase in Satoshi Bold (~48px, charcoal):

- Generous vertical whitespace between blocks — match the winner's density.
- Icons in EHN green #39B54A, simple line-drawn (not emoji).

**Slide 4: CTA & close**
- Background: charcoal (#2C2C2C) or dark sage to create contrast.
- Centred headline in Satoshi Bold, ~80px, off-white: "Reconise the pattern?"
- Subline in Satoshi Medium, ~45px, off-white: "Your perimenopause may need a different approach."
- Small line in Satoshi Medium, ~38px, EHN green #39B54A: "Let's work through it together."
- Bottom: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" (Satoshi Bold, ~40px, EHN green #39B54A).
- Small logo lockup (EHN icon, unobtrusive, top-right or bottom).
- CTA button or text in soft cream background (optional visual container around "Elemental Health & Nutrition").

**Overall palette:**
- Primary: EHN green #39B54A (headlines, accents, CTA, logo).
- Secondary: soft sage green (~A8B8A8) or soft teal/slate-blue (~5A8FA3) for curves — chosen to harmonize with green, never clash.
- Backgrounds: cream (#F5F1EC), charcoal (#2C2C2C) — warm, complementary, clinical.
- Text: Satoshi Bold (headlines, accents), Satoshi Medium (body, supporting lines) — never sub-36px text.

**Legibility + hierarchy:**
- Headline: ~95–110px (Satoshi Bold).
- Subline/supporting: ~45–50px (Satoshi Medium).
- Body text on callouts: ~40px+ (Satoshi Medium).
- Small text (labels, credits): ~32–36px minimum (Satoshi Medium).
- All text readable on cream and charcoal backgrounds — no contrast issues.

The first major physiological shift at perimenopause isn't hot flushes — it's progesterone. This anti-inflammatory, mood-stabilising, histamine-regulating hormone drops rapidly, and that alone can trigger joint ache, anxiety, brain fog, bloating, and histamine intolerance in women who are susceptible.

Understanding this pattern changes how we manage the transition. Rather than riding it out, we can work with your body's actual biochemistry — calming inflammation, supporting mood stability, and addressing the micronutrient demands that come with hormonal change.

If your perimenopause feels more complex than you expected, there's usually a reason. We'd love to help you sort it.

Book an appointment to explore a functional medicine approach to your hormones.

Podcast/interview studio aesthetic, but branded as a clinical consultation room.
- Foreground: leave generous whitespace on left and right (20–30% margin).
- Her face and shoulders fill roughly 40–50% of the frame; upper body visible.

COLOUR PALETTE:
- Primary anchor: EHN green #39B54A — use as an accent bar or side border (thin vertical stripe on left or right edge, or as a subtle underlay behind a text overlay).
- Secondary palette: Sage green (muted, warm-neutral — #B5C9A8 or similar), soft cream (#F5F2F0), warm charcoal (#3C3C3C), and white (#FFFFFF). No purple, orange, or bright florals — keep the mood clinical, warm, and earthy.
- Background: white or soft cream studio setting (matching the winner's bright minimalism, NOT the competitor's dark palette).
- Potted plant: choose a sage or muted green to echo #39B54A without competing.

TEXT OVERLAY (minimal, high-contrast against the studio background):
- Headline (Satoshi Bold, ~95px relative scale, one word in green #39B54A italic): positioned in upper-left or upper-right quadrant, overlaying a semi-transparent soft cream or charcoal (20–30% opacity) card/banner. Example structure: "Your longevity *starts* today" — with "starts" in green italic.

- No on-frame CTA text (let the caption drive the call-to-action).

- Warm, editorial, clinical-but-approachable.
- Whitespace-rich (40–50% negative space outside the subject).
- Soft, intimate lighting matching the podcast-studio aesthetic but branded as a functional-medicine consultation.

Layout: Clinical/anatomical element positioned LEFT side of frame, rendered in muted tones (soft sage, grey-blue) against a deep charcoal background (warm-dark, not pure black). Generous negative space and documentary feel. Headline text (2–3 SHORT words) positioned BOTTOM-RIGHT, in Satoshi Bold: PRIMARY word in EHN green #39B54A (~95px+), secondary/supporting words in white or cream (>=36px).

Colour anchor: EHN green #39B54A as the visual hero — a thin accent line, border highlight, or subtle glow on the clinical element, ensuring green feels intentional and anchors the design. NO green background; green appears as accent only.

Secondary palette: Soft sage (#a8b8a0), warm cream (#f5f1e8), muted blue-grey (#7a8e9e), and the charcoal background — all chosen to harmonize with green and complement the clinical mood. No clashing warm tones (no orange, red, or purple).

Typography: Satoshi Bold for the headline (700 weight), one meaningful word in green #39B54A italic or solid; any subline or body copy in Satoshi Medium (500) in white, cream, or charcoal, >=40px.

Overall feel: Myth-busting, documentary, clinician-credible, slightly provocative. Whitespace is the hero; text is minimal and punchy. The clinical element feels authentic and grounded, not stock. This layout is ready to be grafted onto any myth-bust or functional-medicine topic by swapping the clinical element image and headline words while keeping the colour and composition locked.

posts.caption:
We're taught that early detection is everything — but there's a hard truth: screening tells you that something exists. It doesn't stop it from developing in the first place.

Functional medicine flips the script. Rather than waiting to catch disease, we ask: what creates health? What builds resilience? Prevention isn't a test result — it's the daily choices that keep disease from taking root.

If you're ready to move beyond screening into true prevention, let's talk.

#FunctionalMedicine #Prevention #HealthAdvocacy #AdeLIVE #EHN

posts.caption:
You've probably heard it: skip meals to "reset" your metabolism. But here's what actually happens — intermittent fasting without the right nutrition foundation can leave you stuck in energy-conservation mode. Your body doesn't distinguish between intentional fasting and food insecurity; it simply holds tighter to stored fuel.

Real metabolic resilience comes from consistent, whole-food nourishment. When you eat regularly and choose nutrient-dense meals, your body learns it's safe to spend energy on digestion, repair, and growth.

If you're thinking about changing your eating pattern, let's talk about what works *for you*. Book a consultation and we'll map a plan that honours both your goals and your metabolism.

#IntermittentFasting #MetabolismMyths #FunctionalNutrition #WholeFoods #NutritionConsultation #EastwoodAdelaide

Canvas: single square card (1080 x 1080px).

Background: soft cream (#F5F3F0) to harmonize with EHN green #39B54A and evoke clinical warmth without sterility.

Small circular avatar placeholder (healthcare professional or EHN logo mark, ~80px diameter) on left, with "EHN Clinicians" text to the right in Satoshi Medium 40px, charcoal. No verified checkmark needed — keep it understated and grounded.

Headline section (~20% density): Bold hook in Satoshi Bold, ~95–100px on the 1080 canvas. Primary text in charcoal; ONE meaningful word in green #39B54A italic for visual anchor. Example layout: 
"BREAKING: Six Biomarkers [that word in green italic]
Redefining Wellness"
Keep headline to 2 lines maximum. Lead with the stat/urgency, green word as the pivot.

Listicle body (middle ~40% of card): Six bulleted items in Satoshi Medium 40px, charcoal on cream. Use a small green diamond (●, #39B54A) as the bullet, not blue. Each line is a short phrase (e.g., "Lipopolysaccharide (LPS): gut barrier integrity" or "Zonulin: intestinal permeability marker"). Keep each bullet to one short line; do not wrap. Tight line-height (1.2–1.3) to maintain density and scannability. No emoji — let green diamonds do the visual work.

Footer copy (bottom ~20% of card): Two short paragraphs (Satoshi Medium, 40px, charcoal). First paragraph: 1–2 sentences on why these markers matter (clinical credibility, functional medicine frame). Second paragraph: 1–2 sentences framing it as a next step (no fear-mongering, warm invitation to learn more). Total ~80–100 words max.

Closing line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in Satoshi Medium 40px, green #39B54A, bottom right or bottom centre. Small EHN logo mark optional (unobtrusive, <40px).

Spacing & hierarchy: Match the winner's whitespace ratio — generous margins (60–80px left/right), tight listicle density, breathing room around the headline. The card should feel calm, scannable, clinical-but-warm.

Color palette lock: Green #39B54A as primary anchor (headline word, bullets, closing line). Cream #F5F3F0 background. Charcoal #2C2C2C for all body text and supporting copy. No secondary accent needed — green + cream + charcoal = EHN signature.

posts.build_brief:
Format: vertical reel/short-form video (1080×1920, 9:16).

Canvas & composition:
- Shoot in a real, intimate bathroom or bedroom setting at dusk/early evening, dimmed lighting with ONE warm source (soft table lamp or bedside light, mimicking candlelight warmth but grounded in the client's actual home).
- Subject in silhouette or soft profile (dark neutral clothing—charcoal, sage, navy), standing contemplatively in a moment of pause (hand near face, looking toward the light source, or seated on edge of bed). No talking head; the pose conveys quiet introspection.
- Whitespace & composition: centre the figure slightly off-centre in frame; allow generous negative space (especially upper half) for text overlay.
- Mood: low-light, moody, warm (amber/cream tone from the lamp), contemplative—avoid cold blue or harsh lighting. The visual should feel safe, ritualistic, calming.

Text overlay:
- Hook line (centre-top, ~95px+ headline scale, Satoshi Bold): "You were today years old when you learnt..." — ONE word in EHN green #39B54A italic (e.g., "*learnt*" or "*realised*"). Generous leading, clean serif-like whitespace.
- Transition line (mid-frame, smaller hierarchy, ~50–60px relative, Satoshi Medium, charcoal): "...screens after sunset stop your sleep before it starts."
- Supporting micro-line (lower-mid, ~40–45px, Satoshi Medium, soft charcoal or sage): "Here's why." (or a minimal prompt to keep attention on the visual).

Colour palette (EHN-anchored):
- Primary visual anchor: EHN green #39B54A as the highlighted word in the headline (italic).
- Secondary colours: warm cream, soft sage, charcoal (the neutral tones of the room), soft amber glow from the lamp (natural, not over-saturated).
- Background: the natural room tones (muted cream wall, charcoal shadows, warm lamp glow)—never pure black, never the competitor's amber palette exactly. Keep it grounded and editorial.
- Text: white or off-white on dark areas; charcoal or deep sage on lighter areas. Ensure >=36px floor; avoid tiny subtext.

Typography:
- Headline: Satoshi Bold, ~95px+ (one meaningful word in green #39B54A italic).
- Body/transition: Satoshi Medium, ~50–60px, charcoal or deep sage.
- Micro-prompt: Satoshi Medium, ~40–45px, soft charcoal or sage.

Feel: Clinical-but-warm, editorial, grounded. The reel should feel like a quiet "aha moment" (the hook), not a shouted revelation. The lighting and pose suggest safety, ritual, and nervous-system ease—the opposite of overstimulation.

posts.caption:
Most of us scroll right up until lights out—and then wonder why we're wired at midnight.

Here's the thing: blue light from screens tells your pineal gland it's still daytime. Your melatonin production stalls. Your nervous system stays in "on" mode. And sleep? It gets harder.

A functional-medicine view of sleep isn't just "get more rest"—it's about signalling to your body when day ends. Even a screen-free wind-down from 8pm (or 1–2 hours before bed) can shift your sleep depth and how you feel the next morning.

If you're caught in the "wired but tired" loop, we can help you rebuild that rhythm. Book in for a chat about your sleep patterns—let's find what works for your nervous system.
